rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for miscellaneous unwanted physical things, especially household clutter.

example.english: The room at home is piled up with junk.
example.jyutping: uk1 kei2 gaan1 fong2 deoi1 mun5 zo2 zaap6 mat6

rows.note: Use this for things treated as worthless or low-quality, including junk food; for ordinary mixed clutter, 雜物 is more neutral.

example.english: Eat less of this junk food.
example.traditional: 呢啲垃圾食物少食啲啦。
example.jyutping: ni1 di1 laap6 saap3 sik6 mat6 siu2 sik6 di1 laa1

rows.note: Use this for nonsense or an answer that is meaningless rubbish rather than merely incorrect.

example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 gong2 di1 fai3 waa6 laa1

rows.note: Use this general noun for narcotic drugs; it does not by itself specify heroin.

example.english: He was arrested for selling junk.
example.traditional: 佢因為販賣毒品畀人拉咗。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jan1 wai6 faan3 maai6 duk6 ban2 bei2 jan4 laai1 zo2
